newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares ease 0.32 pct in sharply lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares ease 0.32 pct in sharply lower volume.

text.p: Istanbul stocks dropped slightly in profit-taking on Tuesday after recent sharp gains fuelled by hopes ahead of Monday's approval of the new secularist coalition government, brokers said.
They said a correction was awaited today but the market kept up its political hopes that the new government will win a forthcoming confidence vote in parliament.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,851, down six points or 0.32 percent from Monday's all-time high close of 1,857. It had gained 2.31 percent yesterday on top of last week's 10.5 percent surge.
Trade volume more than halved to 24.76 trillion lira from Monday's 53.02 trillion.

"The index moved in a tight margin today with selective activity. I expect volume and trend to improve tomorrow because there was a late recovery today. The index will probably drift sideways until the confidence vote," said Zuhal Topaloglu from Ekinciler securities.

The secularist coalition of conservative leader Mesut Yilmaz who officially became the new prime minister after President Suleyman Demirel's approval of his cabinet on Monday, will face a confidence vote on July 12.
Yilmaz's alliance is a minority coalition of two right- and one left-wing parties, supported by another left-wing party.

Yilmaz has predicted that he would win the vote with a bigger-than-expected margin with the help of the latest defections from the alliance of former Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his conservative ally Tansu Ciller.

Of the 246 issues traded, falls outdid rises by 114 to 75 while 57 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial edged up 0.12 percent to 1,731, the IMKB Services dropped 1.07 percent to 1,854 and the IMKB Financial firmed 0.15 percent to 2,014.

Actives were led by state oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 86,000, T.Isbank's C series, up 1,000 lira to 59,000, Turkish Airlines, down 500 lira to 42,000 and utilities Cukurova Elektrik, down 10,000 lira to 255,000 lira. They made up 28.1 percent of the total turnover.
